mcpServer.title: AI Assistant (MCP Server)
mcpServer.description: Lets AI assistants (e.g. Claude) read and, for selected tools, write your financial data via the standard MCP protocol. The server is built into Moony and listens on this computer only (127.0.0.1). Note: whatever an AI client reads will be processed by that client — usually in its provider's cloud. Enable only for clients you trust. The app must be unlocked, because the database is encrypted.
mcpServer.enableHint: Serves MCP at a local URL, accessible only while Moony is unlocked
mcpServer.tokenHint: Sent as an Authorization: Bearer header. Treat it like a password.
mcpServer.regenerateHint: Regenerating invalidates every client configuration that uses the current token.
mcpServer.tokenRegenerated: Token regenerated — update your client configurations
mcpServer.portHint: Change only if the default port conflicts with another app. Valid range 1024–65535.
mcpServer.desktopNote: Claude Desktop cannot reach local HTTP servers directly, so this config uses the standard mcp-remote bridge (requires Node.js).
mcpServer.jsonNote: For clients with native HTTP transport support (e.g. .mcp.json in Claude Code projects).
mcpServer.updateFailed: Failed to update MCP server setting
mcpServer.summary: Connect AI assistants such as Claude to your data through a local server. Optional.

dangerZone.title: Danger Zone
dangerZone.confirmDescription: This action cannot be undone. This will permanently delete your account and remove all your data from this device. Since Moony is a local-only app, there is no data on our servers to delete.
dangerZone.backupFirst: Tip: make a backup first (Settings → Data and backups) — it is the only way to get this data back.
dangerZone.deleteAllHint: Removes the profile and the whole database on this computer. Backups saved outside the app stay.

privacy.analyticsHint: Helps us improve the app. Includes screen views and app version. No personal or financial data.
privacy.analyticsUnavailable: This build was made without an analytics key, so nothing is sent and there is nothing to switch on.

data.title: Data and backups
data.description: Where your data lives and how to keep a copy of it.
data.restoreConfirmTitle: Replace your data with this backup?
data.restoreConfirmDescription: Backup from {{date}} (Moony {{version}}, {{attachments}} attachments, {{size}}). Your current data is moved to a "pre-restore" folder inside the data folder, not deleted. Moony will lock afterwards; unlock with the password that was in use when the backup was created.
data.restoreNewer: This backup was created by a newer version of Moony and cannot be restored with this version.
data.restoredDescription: Moony will now lock. Unlock with the backup's password.
data.hint: A backup contains the encrypted database, the key files (salt, key.enc, recovery.enc) and your attachments. It can only be opened with your password or recovery key — keep it somewhere safe, for example an external drive or your own cloud storage.
data.exportHint: Every table in one JSON file.
data.verifyHint: Checks the integrity of the encrypted database.

autoLock.title: Auto-lock
autoLock.description: Lock Moony after a period without activity, so an unattended computer does not leave your finances open. This setting applies to this device only.
autoLock.label: Lock automatically after inactivity
autoLock.hint: Moony also locks when the computer wakes from sleep after that time. You can always lock it by hand from the sidebar.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: Moony can ask GitHub whether a newer version is available. None of your financial data is sent.
updates.autoCheckHint: Checks once per session, after you unlock Moony. This setting applies to this device only.
